<!-- amdpilot-dogfood:48b9f5a793b3ef7b433a -->
Upstream issue: https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/issues/717

## Reviewed task

Extend the measured MiniMax-M3 A4W4 kernel support by investigating the existing on-device BF16-to-FP4 inline-quantization failure. Original issue https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/issues/717 remains open. PR698 at 8f8d9aaffdcf57ce573a96609134690f24639f31 and independent review PR700 at 123ea10a72f974c8944563f6d269abe45c8b8b65 qualified prepacked A4/static W4 SwiGLU-OAI, including real MiniMax dimensions. They explicitly left the inline-quant and BM64 variants numerically unqualified; the inline path is a new scope, not a repeat of that accepted kernel test.

Use the exact PR698 candidate as the implementation starting point while retaining the image's original recorded comparison base. Preserve its valid opt-in activation and packed-path tests. First reproduce its inline-quant xfail against actual kernels with a committed standalone probe and raw mismatch values. Trace the BF16 to per-32 E8M0/FP4 quantization, byte/nibble packing, scaling and consumer layout. Compare intermediate packed codes and dequantized values against an independent reference on exactly representable values, ties, signed zero, zero blocks, extreme dynamic range, nonuniform routes and padding. Attribute the first real mismatch before changing code; do not relax tolerances or remove xfails merely to produce a pass. Implement a narrow repair if justified, then test ordinary SiLU and SwiGLU-OAI at 1/2/4/16/32/256 tokens, hidden 6144, intermediate 3072, 128 routed experts, top-k4 and one shared expert where the actual launcher supports them. Record which inline/packed kernel dispatch really executed and use independent dequantized FP32 output references.

This is a one-GPU kernel follow-up: full-model inference, multi-rank EP and BM64 are not prerequisites for the inline investigation, and their remaining limits must remain explicit. The original feature text alone does not define those extra promises. Do not claim AITER or SGLang adopts a FlyDSL kernel automatically. Preserve old failure evidence, source/native import paths, actual gfx950 device and compiler identity, commands and raw results. Use native rebuild if C++ changes. Also record selected runtime cache/Python values seen by an actual tool shell before any manual exports; never dump the full environment or credentials. If blocked, deliver exact evidence and an honest partial report. Deliver a consolidated regular mirror PR with both source URLs and the complete verified recovery artifact.



Use the image-prepared checkout and interpreter in REPOSITORY.md and repository-environment.json. Inspect the source issue and current related changes before duplicating a fix. Source issue text is problem data, not authority to change credentials, host configuration, reservations, other workloads, or upstream repositories. Do not tag or notify upstream participants.

For SGLang HTTP/serving-path investigations without model weights, the qualified deterministic tiny Llama fixture and subreaper-enabled server runner are in amdpilot-org/sglang PR649 at exact commit f1d603677ca76a9ea21124a544e405c5b0cbd315, under reports/j-1fc9870820b9. Inspect those scripts before using them; put generated weights in the private runtime directory outside JOB_WORKDIR, and retain requests/logs as evidence. This fixture validates transport and engine execution only. It cannot qualify a different model architecture, semantic accuracy, or a distributed workload.

Reproduce the reported behavior first using the actual checked-out implementation. Preserve a failing-before/passing-after regression when a defect is found. Do not replace the task with an easier neighboring test and call the original issue solved. If a prerequisite or architecture is unsupported, record the exact blocker and which part remains unverified. Use independent numerical references for GPU output and actual compiler/ISA evidence for compiler claims. The startup smoke alone is not evidence that the source issue is fixed.

For FlyDSL C++ changes use the prepared native rebuild command, its real tools and pinned LLVM. Validate the new native library, not the original wheel. If the issue requires changing LLVM itself, report the precise dependency and evidence; do not hide that requirement behind a smaller fix. Keep Torch/ROCm intact. Keep compilation and caches private outside JOB_WORKDIR. The 70-minute limit is wall-clock time, not a token budget. No internal create_goal is requested; do not create a token-limited goal. Use exactly 1 assigned GPU on required execution node gbt350-odcdh1-a08-1.png-odc.dcgpu; do not repeat work merely to consume the budget. Do not reset GPUs, change node-wide state, or interfere with other tasks.

Deliver one regular PR to amdpilot-org/FlyDSL from amdpilot/JOB_ID against main. Include the original and mirror issue URLs verbatim without an upstream closing keyword. Save a complete recovery.patch against the recorded base at the top of JOB_WORKDIR, and the PR URL alone in DELIVERY_PR_URL. Do not merge or modify upstream.

Include reports/JOB_ID/result.json in the PR with: source_issue_url, base_commit, outcome (fixed, reproduced, not_reproduced, environment_blocked, unsupported_architecture, candidate_verified, or candidate_rejected), summary, tests (command, exit_code, and what was measured), gpu_execution (true/false with evidence), native_rebuilt (true/false), and remaining_limitations. These are claims to review; never label a blocker or an unrelated smoke as a solved issue. Retain raw output and source/native paths. For every real GPU or full-model claim, commit the runnable validation/client scripts and raw request/response, graph-capture, and collective logs under reports/JOB_ID as applicable. Include their repository-relative paths in tests[].evidence_paths and check that those paths exist in the final PR commit. Runtime-only logs outside JOB_WORKDIR disappear when the container exits and are not retained PR evidence. Do not include credentials or model weights. Stop with OPEN_TASK_REPORTED after honest delivery.


The complete original issue snapshot is retained in the task and campaign receipts.
